ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a rectangle, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; diagonals AC and BD intersect at F. According to the problem requirements, focus on triangle ADB formed by A, D, and B, where AD is the upper side of the rectangle, AB is the left side of the rectangle, and BD is the diagonal. Because ABCD is a rectangle, ∠DAB is a right angle, m∠DAB = 90°. Reasoning: In triangle ADB, the sum of the three interior angles is 180°. The problem gives m∠ADB = 4x + 8, m∠DBA = 6x + 12, plus m∠DAB = 90, so: (4x + 8) + (6x + 12) + 90 = 180. Combining like terms gives 10x + 110 = 180, therefore 10x = 70, x = 7.

raw_record.question_text: Quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle. If $m\angle ADB = 4x + 8$ and $m\angle DBA = 6x + 12$, find x.

method.method_draft: Use triangle ADB. From the image, focus on diagonal BD and the triangle with vertices A, D, and B; because ABCD is a rectangle, angle DAB is a right angle. From the text, substitute m∠ADB = 4x + 8 and m∠DBA = 6x + 12. Apply the triangle angle-sum rule: (4x + 8) + (6x + 12) + 90 = 180, so 10x + 20 = 90 and x = 7.
